newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Gunmen slay 3 jail officials in northwest Colombia.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen slay 3 jail officials in northwest Colombia.

text.p: Three prison officials were shot dead by motorcycle assassins wielding high-powered assault rifles in the trouble-torn northwest Colombian city of Medellin on Monday night, police said.

The men were killed as they drove by car through a western district of the country's third largest city which had been rocked by a devastating car bomb earlier in the day, resulting in the death of one woman and injuries to 48 other people.

A police spokesman said one of the dead, a retired police major, worked in Medellin's Bellavista jail but was soon due to transfer to a jail in Cali, home to the mighty Cali drug cartel. Another man was the director of the prisons service in southwest Valle del Cauca province, whose main city is Cali. The third man killed was also a prison officer.
Four unidentified gunmen on two motorcycles riddled the trio's car with bullets using AK-47 assault weapons, the police spokesman said.
There was no immediate indication whether the killings were linked to the explosion of 120 pounds (50 kg) of dynamite packed into a minibus in a residential area of Medellin.

President Ernesto Samper and his Defence Minister Juan Carlos Esguerra blamed the blast on narco-terrorists retaliating against Congress' approval last week of a tough new law to strip drug kingpins of their multibillion-dollar fortunes.
